archetypes.disclaimer: Archetypes are original PersonalityDNA descriptive summaries of trait patterns. They are not validated psychological types; most people show elements of several archetypes.

growth: Share your ideas, not only support for others' ideas
primary.name: The Collaborator
primary.summary: Tends to value cooperation and practical, familiar ways of working with others.

growth: Try one small new approach at a time
Ask what problem a proposed change is solving
secondary.name: The Organizer
secondary.summary: Tends to value proven methods, order and dependable routines.

methodology.attribution: Items from the International Personality Item Pool (ipip.ori.org), public domain.
methodology.band_note: Lower is below 40, middle is 40-60, higher is above 60 on that 0-100 scale.
limitations: Results describe how you rated yourself today. Self-ratings can shift with mood, context and time.
Scores show where your answers fall on the 1-5 response scale. They are not percentiles and do not compare you with other people, because no reference population data is used.
This is not a clinical or diagnostic tool and says nothing about mental health conditions.
Archetypes are original descriptive summaries, not scientifically validated types. Most people show elements of several.
Personality alone does not determine career success, relationship outcomes or suitability for any role. Do not use these results for hiring or other decisions about people.
methodology.negative_emotionality_note: The instrument measures Emotional Stability. Negative Emotionality (often called Neuroticism) is the same scale in the reverse direction: 100 minus Emotional Stability.
references: Goldberg, L. R. (1992). The development of markers for the Big-Five factor structure. Psychological Assessment, 4(1), 26-42.

Goldberg, L. R. (1999). A broad-bandwidth, public domain, personality inventory measuring the lower-level facets of several five-factor models. In I. Mervielde et al. (Eds.), Personality Psychology in Europe, Vol. 7 (pp. 7-28). Tilburg University Press.

Goldberg, L. R., Johnson, J. A., Eber, H. W., Hogan, R., Ashton, M. C., Cloninger, C. R., & Gough, H. G. (2006). The International Personality Item Pool and the future of public-domain personality measures. Journal of Research in Personality, 40, 84-96.
methodology.scoring_summary: Each answer is scored 1-5. Negatively worded items are reversed (6 minus the answer). Each trait score is the average of its items, shown on a 0-100 scale where 0 means every answer was at the low end and 100 means every answer was at the high end.

traits.description: Sociability, assertiveness and energy from social interaction.
growth: Plan how you will share your views in group settings
traits.name: Extraversion
traits.summary: You describe yourself as quieter and more reserved, often preferring smaller settings.

traits.description: Warmth, empathy, cooperation and consideration for others.
growth: Practise stating your own needs clearly
traits.name: Agreeableness
traits.summary: You describe yourself as warm, caring and attentive to other people's feelings.

growth: Allow room for change in plans
Notice when high standards cost more than they return
traits.name: Conscientiousness
traits.summary: You describe yourself as organised, prepared and attentive to detail.

traits.description: How calm and even-tempered you describe yourself in everyday situations. The reverse direction is called Negative Emotionality (Neuroticism).
growth: Try a short routine for stressful moments, such as pausing to name what you feel
If stress feels overwhelming, consider speaking with a qualified professional
traits.name: Emotional Stability
traits.summary: You describe yourself as experiencing everyday stress and emotional ups and downs fairly often.

traits.description: Curiosity, imagination and interest in ideas and new experiences.
growth: Notice which situations draw out your curiosity, and seek more of them where useful
traits.name: Openness
traits.summary: You describe a mix of practicality and curiosity, depending on the situation.
